clue.text: Right to reject poet's third book as inaccessible?

parts.note: R is the usual abbreviation for right

indicators.note: rejecting something throws it back, so the word is turned around

parts.note: a tome is a large book

indicators.note: third points to a single letter counted from the front of the word

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses a poet's third volume as too obscure for readers.
explanation.walkthrough: R, then the book turned round (EMOT), then E gives REMOTE; the book is rejected, not the poet.
explanation.definitionFit: A remote place is far away and hard to reach, so it is a near synonym.

clue.text: Pilot has crashed into medical centre

indicators.note: a crashed vehicle is wrecked and scattered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A pilot has flown his plane into a medical building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has crashed' reads as the story's verb, but it is the signal to rearrange the letters of pilot and has.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospital is a place where patients receive treatment from doctors and nurses.

clue.text: Dug round opening in consecrated ground

indicators.note: going round something encloses it, so one word wraps the other

parts.note: mined means dug out of the earth

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone dug around the entrance to a churchyard or other holy ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'consecrated ground' reads as one phrase, but ground stands alone as the definition, a past participle of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Minced meat has been put through a grinder, so minced and ground mean the same in the kitchen.

clue.text: Piled up special riding kit to give to leaders of equestrian display

parts.note: S is a standard abbreviation for special
tack is the saddle, bridle and other gear for riding a horse

indicators.note: leaders are the ones at the front, so only the opening letters count

parts.note: first letters of equestrian and display

explanation.surface: Stable hands heap up gear for the riders at a horse show.
explanation.walkthrough: Tack is the horse-riding word for saddle and bridle, which fits the equestrian scene the surface paints.
explanation.definitionFit: Things stacked have been placed one on top of another in a heap or pile.

clue.text: Large hole made by large box found by river

parts.note: a crate is a big wooden packing case
R is the usual abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A big pit has been left where a heavy chest was dumped beside a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A crater is a bowl-shaped pit, as left by a meteorite or a bomb.

clue.text: Fish swallowing Jonah's heart seen, strangely, to get smaller

indicators.note: what swallows something takes it inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: the cod is a common sea fish

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letter
done strangely means done in an odd order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A big fish swallows Jonah and is seen to shrink, a twist on the Bible story.
explanation.walkthrough: Jonah suggests the whale, but the fish here is just a cod, with only the middle of Jonah inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense is to compress or reduce something into a smaller space or shorter form.

clue.text: Arranged to get Ian drug deal

indicators.note: arranging puts things into a new order, so the letters are reordered

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone set up a drugs deal for a man called Ian.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' and 'deal' sound like one story, but the first is the signal and the last is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal with someone in business is to bargain and reach terms, which is to negotiate.

clue.text: A nurse inhales oxygen and another gas

indicators.note: breathing something in takes it inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: RGN stands for Registered General Nurse, a British nursing qualification
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A nurse breathes in oxygen along with a second gas in a hospital ward.
explanation.walkthrough: The O goes between the G and N of RGN. 'another' is fair because oxygen, already named, is also a gas.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a noble gas, one of the inert elements found in small amounts in air.

clue.text: Nonsense talked by one crowing next to flower?

parts.note: the poppy is a red flower

explanation.surface: Silly talk from a rooster standing beside a bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: The flower comes first in the answer even though the clue names the bird first: one crowing sits next to the flower, after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Poppycock is an informal word for foolish talk or rubbish, the same as nonsense spoken.

clue.text: Analyse fertiliser close to dairy

parts.note: a stud is a male animal kept for breeding, playfully a fertiliser

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is used

explanation.surface: A farmer examines the manure spread near the milking shed.
explanation.walkthrough: Fertiliser suggests manure, but here it is one who fertilises: a stud animal used for breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: To study something is to examine it closely in detail, the same as analysing it.

clue.text: Cooking facility used by topless witches

indicators.note: without a top means the first letter is cut off

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches

explanation.surface: Half-naked witches share a stove for their brews.
explanation.walkthrough: Witches suggests a cauldron, but the group word for witches loses its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven is the enclosed heated compartment of a stove used for baking and roasting.

clue.text: Soprano and tenor in poverty prepared to have babies

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it is placed inside

parts.note: need is a state of poverty or want
S and T are the usual abbreviations for soprano and tenor

explanation.surface: Two poor singers get ready to start a family.
explanation.walkthrough: Birds that have nested have built a nest ready for laying eggs; in people it means preparing the home for a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesting is the instinct to prepare a home before birth, so nested means got ready for offspring.

clue.text: Locality with space for opening of volleyball clubs

definitions.note: the answer is a plural noun meaning the surrounding area

parts.note: an en is a printer's space, half an em wide

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A neighbourhood offers room for starting up volleyball teams.
explanation.walkthrough: Clubs suggests sports teams beside volleyball, but they are golf clubs. EN is a printing measure of space.
explanation.definitionFit: Environs are the surrounding district or neighbourhood of a place, a vicinity or locality.

clue.text: Doctor catching a fish for sweetheart

indicators.note: catching something holds it, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: Dr is the abbreviated title for a doctor
the ling is a long sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A doctor lands a fish to give to his beloved.
explanation.definitionFit: Darling and sweetheart are both affectionate terms for someone dearly loved.

clue.text: A correspondent welcoming the beginning of chatty part of letter

indicators.note: welcoming someone takes them in, so one piece goes inside the other
the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A letter writer opens with a friendly, chatty section of the letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Letter means a written message on the surface, but in the definition it is a letter of the alphabet, as in typography.
explanation.definitionFit: An ascender is the stroke of a lower-case character that rises above the main body, as in b, d or h.

clue.text: Want to give maiden name to daughter

parts.note: née introduces a married woman's maiden name
D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A parent wishes to pass a family maiden name on to their daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Want and need both mean a lack of something required, as nouns or verbs.

clue.text: Furious to see untidy English garden

indicators.note: an untidy thing is messy and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A tidy-minded gardener is livid at the state of an English garden.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone enraged is filled with rage, which is to say extremely angry or furious.

clue.text: Dancing bear, 16, climbing in Scottish city

indicators.note: a dancing thing moves about, so the letters are moved around
in a down clue climbing goes upwards, so the word is read from bottom to top

explanation.surface: A performing bear climbs about in a city in Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 16 brings in its answer, which is then turned upwards as this is a down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen is a city on the north-east coast of Scotland, known as the Granite City.

clue.text: Instruction to keep writing on relative's hat

parts.note: stet is a proofreader's mark meaning let the original text stand

explanation.surface: Someone has written a note on a family member's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: Stet, Latin for let it stand, tells a printer to keep text that was marked for deletion. It sits on top of the relative in a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A Stetson is a wide-brimmed cowboy hat, named after its American maker.

clue.text: Composer's arrangement for butchers

indicators.note: an arrangement of a piece reorders it, so the letters are put in new order

explanation.surface: A musical piece by a composer, arranged for a band of butchers.
explanation.walkthrough: Arrangement is a musical word, so it hides well as the anagram signal next to a composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Schubert was an Austrian composer of symphonies, chamber music and songs.

clue.text: Where men go to ruin pants with a lager top?

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters come out badly ordered
the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Men head to the gents after spilling lager over their trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: Pants is the signal, used in its British slang sense of rubbish; the surface pretends it means trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A urinal is a fixture in a men's toilet, a place where men go to relieve themselves.

clue.text: Conservative pinching the other fellow's idea

indicators.note: pinching something grabs and holds it, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory politician steals a rival's idea.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for has, linking the wordplay to the definition at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A theory is a proposed idea or explanation, a notion held without full proof.

clue.text: Tear into empty takeaway that's fashionable

indicators.note: one thing going into another means it is placed inside
emptying a word takes out its insides, leaving only the outer letters

explanation.surface: Ripping open a finished takeaway carton in the latest style.
explanation.definitionFit: Trendy describes anything in the current fashion or style, so it means fashionable.

clue.text: Learnt about leasing arrangement

indicators.note: about means moved around, so the letters are scattered into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone has found out about the terms of a lease.
explanation.definitionFit: A rental is an agreement to hire property or goods for payment over a set period.

clue.text: Country returning financial help to Northern Ireland

indicators.note: returning goes back the way it came, so the whole string is read backwards

parts.note: aid is help, such as money given to another country
NI is the abbreviation for Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: A nation pays back financial support it was given by Northern Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: The help is joined to Northern Ireland first, then the whole string is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: India is a large nation in South Asia, the second most populous on Earth.

clue.text: Escort coming in at 10 (Danish time)

parts.note: Dan is an abbreviation for Danish
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A companion turns up at ten o'clock, Copenhagen time.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket looks like a time zone, but each word in it is just another piece added on in order.
explanation.definitionFit: An attendant accompanies someone to help or guard them, as an escort does.

clue.text: Envelope cannot contain nut

indicators.note: the run of words contains the letters within them, across the word break

parts.note: letters running across the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An envelope is too small to hold a nut.
explanation.definitionFit: The pecan is a sweet nut from a hickory tree of the southern United States.

clue.text: Fashion model glad to get first prize

indicators.note: to fashion is to shape or make, so the letters are formed into something new

explanation.surface: A catwalk model is delighted to win the top award.
explanation.walkthrough: Fashion model reads as one phrase, a catwalk model, but fashion is a verb telling you to rework the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A gold medal is awarded to the winner of a competition, the top place.
